text: To throng with something is to be crowded with it — packed, not just busy. The article says Labuan Bajo now throngs with diving shops, restaurants and hotels, which means the town has filled up tightly with tourist businesses. As a noun, a throng is a dense crowd of people.

Dismay is the shaken, discouraged feeling that bad and unexpected news leaves behind. Here the four deaths in December caused widespread dismay, meaning people across the region were upset by something nobody had seen coming. It is heavier than disappointment but quieter than anger.

To implement a plan is to carry it out and do the real work that turns an announced idea into something that exists. The tourism authority here was set up to implement the ex-president's ideas: he named the goal, and the organisation had to arrange the hotels, roads and permits. There is also a noun implement meaning a tool, but the verb is what you meet in writing like this.

A cap here is not a hat. It is an upper limit somebody sets on purpose: Komodo's cap of 1,000 tourists a day means the park lets 1,000 in and no more. You will meet the word used this way for spending caps, class-size caps and price caps.

A drive, in this sense, is a big organised push to get something done, and has nothing to do with cars. Indonesia's drive to expand tourism was a national effort with money, plans and officials behind it. Schools and charities run fundraising drives in the same way.

A body can mean an organisation rather than a person. The article calls the Labuan Bajo Flores Tourism Authority a body set up to implement the president's ideas, meaning an official group with one job to do. Governments create bodies like this all the time: a safety body, a sports body, an exam body.

When a place boasts something, it simply has something impressive, and nobody is bragging. Saying the park boasts a unique tourist attraction means it has one. Only people boast in the show-off sense; places and products boast in this neutral one.

To promote something here means to advertise it and push people towards it — not to move up a grade or a job. The tourism authority wants to promote other attractions so visitors spread out instead of all heading for the dragons. Companies promote products the same way.

Remains, used as a noun, means what is physically left of something once it has died: bones, teeth, fossils. The article mentions the discovery of remains of Homo floresiensis on Flores, meaning fossil bones, not leftovers. Archaeologists use the word constantly.

To prompt something is to cause it to happen soon afterwards. The boat accident prompted a temporary closure, so the park shut because of the accident. The word always links a trigger to the reaction it sets off.

To settle in a place is to move there and stay for good — not to sit down or to calm down. The article says Portuguese traders and missionaries settled in the island in the 16th century, meaning they built homes there and their families stayed. People who do this are called settlers.

If conditions are conducive, they help something happen or make it possible. Ms Jemana says that if the weather is not conducive, boats should not be given permission to sail, because the sea is too rough for a safe trip. You will almost always meet the word in this shape: conducive to something.

To mollify someone is to calm them down when they are annoyed. The last line jokes that with luck the dragons will be mollified, as though the lizards were irritated by the crowds and are being soothed by the new limit. Dragons do not actually take offence; the writer is being funny about the cap.

Phenomenal means extraordinary, far beyond normal. The region is struggling to cope with phenomenal growth: visits rose fivefold in ten years, far more than a small town can absorb. It is a strong word, so save it for things that really are remarkable.

Fivefold means five times as much. The ending -fold always works this way, so twofold is double and tenfold is ten times. Visits increasing fivefold in a decade means roughly five times as many people now as ten years ago.

A venomous animal injects poison into you through a bite or a sting. That is different from poisonous, which means harmful if you eat or touch it. Komodo dragons are venomous: a bite pushes venom into the wound, and the venom keeps the blood from clotting.

To lounge is to lie about lazily, relaxed and in no hurry. The article warns that a dragon may lounge around sleepily and still be dangerous, because a resting animal can move fast with no warning. People lounge on sofas, and the word carries that same slack, unbothered picture.

To cope with something is to manage it without being overwhelmed. Saying the region is struggling to cope with phenomenal growth means the roads, boats and hotels cannot keep up with the number of visitors. You cope with a hard week, a crowd, or too much homework.

A species is extinct when every member of it has died and none are left anywhere on Earth. Homo floresiensis is extinct, which is why only its bones remain. The Komodo dragon is not extinct, but with roughly 1,300 adults left it is the kind of animal people worry about.

Missionaries are people sent to a distant place to spread their religion, often running schools or clinics while they are there. The Portuguese missionaries mentioned here reached Flores in the 16th century, and the island's old churches date from that time. The word comes from mission, a job you are sent out to do.

A cyclone is an enormous spinning storm that forms over warm ocean, with winds strong enough to flatten buildings. It is the same kind of storm as a hurricane or a typhoon — the name changes depending on which ocean it forms in. The article lists cyclones among the disasters Komodo dragons have already lived through.

To be at the sharp end of something is to be where it is felt most strongly, because that is where the pressure or the risk lands. Komodo has been at the sharp end of Indonesia's tourism drive, meaning it has taken the full force of the change. Nurses are often described as being at the sharp end of a health crisis.

t: at the end of the day
forms: at the end of the day
text: At the end of the day means in the end, once everything is weighed up — it is not about evening. The writer uses it to say that whatever else the region advertises, what tourists really want is the dragons. It is one of the commonest ways English speakers introduce a final point.

After all signals that the reason for what was just said is coming next. Writing that Labuan Bajo was high on the president's list, and then After all, it boasts a unique attraction, tells you why it was. The same phrase can also mean despite everything, as in She came after all, so check which sense fits.

The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard alive: up to about three metres long, 80kg in weight, with a venomous bite. It lives wild in only one place on Earth, a few small Indonesian islands, and only about 1,300 adults are thought to be left. It is the reason tourists travel to Komodo at all.

Komodo is a small, dry, hilly Indonesian island with no airport, so everyone arrives by sea. It and a few neighbouring islands are the only places in the world where Komodo dragons live wild. The boats, beds and supplies its visitors need come mostly from Labuan Bajo, across the water on Flores.

Komodo National Park is land and sea that Indonesia's government has set aside by law to protect the dragons and the reefs around them. Because it is a park, a government office decides who may enter, charges for tickets and can close it — which is how a limit of 1,000 visitors a day is even possible. It covers Komodo and several nearby islands.

A national park authority is the government office that runs a park day to day: it hires rangers, sells permits, writes the rules and can shut the gates. The article says the tourism authority had urged this office to limit access during the wet season. Every country has a body like it; in the United States it is the National Park Service.

Labuan Bajo is a town on the island of Flores and the jumping-off point for Komodo: visitors arrive there, sleep there, and leave by boat in the morning. The article says it now throngs with diving shops, hotels and coffee spots that have multiplied as visits grew. It is where the money the dragons attract actually lands.

This is the government body Indonesia created to carry out the plan of turning Labuan Bajo and Flores into a major tourist destination. Sisilia Lenita Jemana, quoted in the article, is one of its marketing managers — and notice that she is the one saying the plan worked too well. An organisation set up to bring tourists in is now asking for limits on them.

Flores is a long, mountainous Indonesian island east of Bali, far bigger than Komodo, with active volcanoes and national parks of its own. Labuan Bajo sits at its western tip. Flores is also where the bones of Homo floresiensis were dug up, which is how that species got its name.

Indonesia is a country in South-East Asia made up of more than 17,000 islands, among them Java, Bali, Flores and Komodo. More people live there than in any country except India, China and the United States. Because it sits across the equator, its year divides into a wet and a dry season rather than four seasons.

Bali is the Indonesian island that has long been the country's tourist centre, crowded with beaches, temples and hotels. When President Widodo said he wanted ten new Balis, he meant ten more places earning that kind of money from visitors. Balinese means the people of Bali, or anything belonging to the island.

Joko Widodo, widely known as Jokowi, was president of Indonesia from 2014 until two years before this article was written. He pushed hard to build up tourism outside Bali, hoping for jobs and higher incomes. The plan for Labuan Bajo and Komodo was one of his projects, which is why the tourism authority is described as a body set up to implement his ideas.

Valencia CF is a well-known Spanish football club from the city of Valencia. It appears here because Fernando Martin, one of the four Spanish tourists who died when their tour boat sank, was a coach there. The CF stands for Club de Futbol, Spanish for football club.

Homo floresiensis is an extinct relative of modern humans whose bones were found on Flores about twenty years ago. Adults stood only about a metre tall, which is why newspapers nicknamed them Hobbit man after the small people in Tolkien's books. They were not our species but a separate branch of the human family that died out.

Maritime means to do with the sea, so the maritime authorities are the government officials in charge of boats and shipping. They are the ones who grant or refuse permission to sail, which is why the tourism authority keeps pressing them about the wet season. Coast guards and port officials belong to this group.

Foreign exchange means money from other countries. Each country uses its own currency, so when a visitor from Spain spends euros in Indonesia, Indonesia ends up holding euros it can use to buy things from abroad. That is why the article counts the vast amounts of foreign exchange Bali brings in as a benefit.

Migrant workers are people who move away from home to find work, usually sending money back to their families. Here it means Indonesians from poorer islands who travel to Bali for hotel and restaurant jobs, not people crossing a border between countries. Tourist towns everywhere run on workers like them.

Mass tourism means very large numbers of ordinary travellers visiting the same place, rather than a few rich or adventurous ones. Cheap flights, big hotels and tour boats are what make it possible. The first sentence of the article asks whether the Komodo dragon can survive it.

A supply base is the nearby place that provides everything a destination needs: food, fuel, boats, staff and beds. Labuan Bajo is Komodo's supply base, because Komodo itself has no airport and almost no facilities. Armies and expeditions use the term in exactly the same way.

Portugal, a small country in western Europe, sent ships right across the world in the 1500s to trade in spices, and its traders and priests reached these islands then. That is why Flores has Portuguese place names, old churches and many Catholic families. The tourism authority now wants to promote those historic sites to visitors.

An ice age is a long stretch of time, tens of thousands of years, when Earth was much colder and thick ice covered far more of its land. There have been many, and the most recent one ended about 11,700 years ago. The article's point is that Komodo dragons lived through changes that huge, and may still be undone by tourism.

Kilograms are the metric unit of weight used almost everywhere outside the United States, and 80kg is about 175 pounds — roughly what a grown man weighs. So a full-grown Komodo dragon can be as heavy as an adult human and three metres, or ten feet, long. The article gives the length in both feet and metres.
